items.title: What will war look like after peace?
Palestinian farmers battle settler sabotage to save Hebron crops, livestock
items.description: West Bank farmers defy daily settler attacks, sheep theft, and military restrictions to protect their land.

items.title: Putin, war leader and election campaign chief, prepares Russia for military escalation
items.description: For the first time since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Russians will elect their MPs between September 18 and 20. Orchestrated by the Kremlin, this vote carries no real electoral stakes and serves above all as a tool to rally support for the war effort.

items.title: U.S. Envoys Make First Kyiv Visit Amid Ukraine War Peace Push
items.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled from Moscow, where they held three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday.

items.title: Ukraine-Russia talks: What are the US objectives?
items.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push for peace, more than 4½ years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. We discuss this topic with our guest, John E. Herbst, director of the Eurasia Center at the Atlantic Council…

items.title: US Sanctions Chief Joins Moscow Talks as Putin Cites War Goals
items.description: A US delegation led by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner included Gene Lange, acting head of the US Treasury’s sanctions unit, signaling that sanctions policy was part of diplomatic talks in Moscow. While Lange met with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev rather than Vladimir Putin directly, a White House official confirmed NS…

items.title: Cremlino, 'i colloqui tra Putin e gli inviati Usa estremamente franchi'
items.description: Ushakov: 'Witkoff e Kushner hanno illustrato diverse idee per porre fine alla guerra'

items.title: US Envoys Conclude Moscow Meeting With Putin As Kremlin Cites 'Difficult Situation'
items.description: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have begun their meeting in Moscow with President Vladimir Putin as part of a renewed White House effort to end Russia's war against Ukraine, with the pair set to visit Kyiv afterward.

items.title: Civilians among at least 60 killed in Yemen as ground fighting escalates
items.description: Houthi rebel offensive against government forces on west coast leads to some of deadliest clashes in yearsClashes between Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi rebel movement have killed more than 60 people, including civilians, as the Houthis pushed forward with a military offensive on Yem…

items.title: How the U.S. focus on Iran is fueling a more aggressive Putin
items.description: Trump's top envoys head to Moscow and Kyiv as Putin steps up round the clock bombing of Ukraine. With the U.S. distracted by Iran, is Putin becoming increasingly emboldened?

items.title: Yemen: Fighting intensifies amid Houthi push in the west
items.description: Houthi forces are trying to secure high ground and solidify their control of the entry to the Red Sea in the southwest. The Iran-backed militia abandoned a shaky truce with the Saudi-backed government-in-exile in July.

items.title: 'We expect our sons to be killed,' father of teen shot dead in West Bank tells BBC
items.description: Palestinian teenagers Omar al-Naasan and Khalil Abu Alia were shot dead when Israeli settlers and soldiers entered a village in the occupied West Bank.

items.title: Repeated attacks on humanitarian warehouses put vital medical aid at risk in Ukraine: WHO
items.description: A new airstrike overnight damaged one of the main warehouses used by the World Health Organization (WHO) in Ukraine to store humanitarian medical supplies in the Kyiv region, the UN agency said on Friday.

items.title: How growing Israeli-Turkish tensions led to a strike on a Syrian air base
items.description: Could the growing regional rivalry between Turkey and Israel lead to a military clash? A recent Israeli strike on an air base in northern Syria illustrated the two countries’ conflicting strategic interests, but analysts say neither wants war.
